A bud grows on Hydra's body and detaches as a new individual.

q: One spermatogonium undergoing spermatogenesis ultimately gives rise to how many functional sperm?
why: Meiosis I and II convert 1 spermatogonium into 4 haploid spermatids/sperm.

q: Oogenesis in humans yields how many functional ova per primary oocyte?
why: Unequal cytoplasm division gives only 1 functional ovum plus polar bodies.

q: A sharp LH surge around day 14 of the menstrual cycle triggers:
why: The LH surge causes rupture of the Graafian follicle, releasing the ovum.

q: If ovulation occurs on day 14 and the cycle length is 28 days with no fertilization, menstruation begins again near day:
why: 28-day cycle: menstruation restarts near day 28 after corpus luteum degenerates.

q: Fertilization in humans normally occurs in the:
why: Sperm and ovum fuse in the ampulla of the fallopian tube.

q: The outer layer of the blastocyst that attaches to the endometrium during implantation is the:
why: The trophoblast attaches to and digests into the endometrium, enabling implantation.

q: The hormone mainly responsible for strong uterine contractions leading to parturition is:
why: Posterior pituitary releases oxytocin, which drives labour contractions.

q: Milk ejection (letting-down) from the mammary gland during suckling is caused mainly by:
why: Oxytocin contracts muscle cells around milk glands, ejecting milk; prolactin only makes milk.
